articles.title: Nuevo ataque machista a una tenista: "Espero que te suicides, no estarás a la altura de un hombre, perra"
articles.standfirst: La tenista Jodie Burrage denuncia ante la WTA los despreciables ataques que ha sufrido tras su regreso al circuito
articles.summary: La tenista Jodie Burrage denuncia ante la WTA los despreciables ataques que ha sufrido tras su regreso al circuito
articles.body: La Jodie Burrage ha revelado que ha recibido amenazas de muerte en redes sociales tras disputar su primer partido en el circuito WTA después de 16 meses de ausencia. La tenista británica, que es la número 474 del ránking, fue derrotada en la primera ronda en Chennai por la india Vaishnavi Adkar por 3-6, 6-3, 7-5. Tras la derrota Jodie Burrage (27 años) compartió en su 'stories' de Instagram los ataques que sufrió en redes sociales y los compartió con la WTA. "¡Qué buena bienvenida a mi regreso al circuito! Ya recuerdo por qué me fui. ¿Cuándo van a hacer algo al respecto?", denunció la tenista británica. Algunos de los mensajes más despreciables que sufrió Burrage fueron "eres una cobarde que tira la toalla. De verdad, eres una vergüenza para este deporte. Hoy te han dado una paliza, y eres precisamente la razón por la que el deporte femenino es un chiste", "espero que te vayas a casa y te suicides, porque, sinceramente, es lo mejor que puedes hacer. Nunca estarás a la altura de un hombre, perra" o "muérete y provoca disturbios en las calles". La denuncia de Burrage, número 15 de Gran Bretaña, se produce más de un año después de que otra tenista británica, Katie Boulter, confesara haber recibido también amenazas de muerte a través de las redes sociales. En 2025 Katie Boulter recibió mensajes como "espero que te dé cáncer", "profanaremos la tumba de tu abuela si no está muerta para mañana" o "vete al infierno; he perdido el dinero que me envió mi madre".

articles.title: Hong Kong Open: GB's Mika Stojsavljevic, 17, beats Sofia Kenin for first WTA Tour main-draw win
articles.summary: British teenager Mika Stojsavljevic beats former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin for her first WTA Tour main-draw win.
articles.body:
British teenager Mika Stojsavljevic beat former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin to claim her first WTA Tour main-draw win - despite only having an hour's notice that she would be playing.

The 17-year-old lost in qualifying for the Hong Kong Open but entered the main draw as a lucky loser.

World number 411 Stojsavljevic came through a close deciding set to beat the American 6-3 4-6 6-4.

"I only knew an hour before I was going to be playing. I kind of just went out and swung today," Stojsavljevic said.

"I know she's a Grand Slam champion and it was never going to be an easy match, but I believed in myself and it worked out."

Kenin, 27, has had a torrid time since winning the Melbourne title in 2020 but is still ranked 224 places above the Briton.

Stojsavljevic hit six winners to her opponent's zero and saved three of the eight break points she faced.

It is a second big win of the year for Stojsavljevic, who stunned then world number 56 Talia Gibson at Billie Jean King Cup qualifying in April.

Stojsavljevic started playing tennis aged seven at Ealing Lawn Tennis Club in north-west London after watching her brother practise.

In 2024, she became the first Briton in 15 years to win the US Open junior title.

She reached a high of fifth in the junior world rankings and turned professional in 2025.

Earlier this year, she reached the quarter-finals of the WTA 125 event in Birmingham - the tier that sits below the main Tour.

Stojsavljevic will face world number 67 Zeynep Sonmez in the second round in Hong Kong.

Fellow Briton Katie Boulter's season came to an end with a 7-5 6-4 loss to American Claire Liu at the same tournament.

articles.title: British No. 15 Jodie Burrage reveals horrific social media death threats after losing to India's Vaishnavi Adkar on 16-month WTA return
articles.summary: Jodie Burrage, British tennis player, reveals she received death threats on social media following her defeat at the Chennai Open, sparking outrage and calls for action against online abuse in sports.
articles.body: British tennis player Jodie Burrage has revealed that she received death threats and abusive messages after losing her first WTA Tour singles match in 16 months. The 27-year-old shared screenshots of the messages after her first-round defeat at the Chennai Open, questioning why social media platforms had not done more to protect players.Jodie Burrage shares death threats after Chennai Open defeatBurrage, ranked 474th in the world and Britain's No 15, lost 3-6, 6-3, 7-5 to India's Vaishnavi Adkar in the first round of the Chennai Open. Despite taking the opening set, the British player was unable to prevent Adkar from recovering to win the match in three sets.It was Burrage's first match in the main draw of a WTA Tour event since July 2025, excluding qualifying tournaments. Her previous appearance at that level had ended in a first-round defeat by Catherine McNally at Wimbledon.After the Chennai match, Burrage posted an Instagram story showing a scroll of direct messages she had received. Alongside the video, she wrote: “Nice welcome back to tour. I remember why I left. When will something be done?”She tagged both the WTA and Instagram, directing attention to the abuse and asking what action would be taken against those sending it.One message accused Burrage of being a “quitter” and a “disgrace to the sport”, before attacking women's tennis and telling her to kill herself. It read: “Your [sic] a quitter smh [shake my head]. You truly are a disgrace to the sport. You got your ass whooped today and you are the exact reason women's sports are a joke.“Hope you go home and kill yourself bc [because] honestly that's what's best. You will never compare to a man b***h.”Another pending direct message read: “Die n riot [sic] on the streets”, while a separate message directed at the player said: “F***** [sic] ****”.The messages included personal abuse and encouragement of self-harm, rather than criticism of Burrage's performance. Her post also drew support from fellow players, including Germany's Eva Lys, who shared the issue on Instagram and tagged the WTA, asking: “When will something be done?”Katie Boulter also received death threats after French Open matchBurrage's experience follows a similar case involving fellow British player Katie Boulter, who spoke to BBC Sport in 2025 about receiving death threats and other abusive messages online.Boulter became the target of abuse after losing the first set of her opening-round match against Carole Monnet at the French Open. She went on to win the match, but the result did not prevent users from sending threats to her social media accounts.Screenshots shown to the BBC included one message saying: “Hope you get cancer”. Another threatened to damage her grandmother's grave if she was not dead by the following day, while also referring to “candles and a coffin for your entire family”.A third message read: “Go to hell, I lost money my mother sent me.”The reference to lost money reflected a pattern identified in research into online abuse directed at tennis players. A report by the Signify Group, which monitors threats and abuse through its AI-led threat detection service, found two years ago that angry gamblers were responsible for 48 per cent of posts classified as abusive.More than 12,000 abusive messages targeted female tennis players in 2025The scale of the problem extends beyond individual cases. According to a report published earlier in 2026, female tennis players received more than 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media during 2025.According to the BBC, data from the Signify Group's threat matrix service showed that the number of abusive posts and messages was similar to the figure recorded in 2024. The report also found that angry gamblers accounted for 42 per cent of verified abuse in 2025 and 59 per cent of cases classified as serious abuse.The findings point to gambling-related anger as a significant source of online hostility towards players, although the abuse received by Burrage and Boulter also included threats and misogynistic attacks unrelated to any assessment of their performances.Players have previously called for social media companies to introduce identity verification measures in an effort to make users more accountable for the messages they send. The WTA's player board has also condemned the abuse, describing it as “unacceptable” and warning that its impact on those targeted can be “significant”.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Real Madrid: Rafael Nadal appointed to LaLiga club's board of directors
articles.summary: Real Madrid hailed retired tennis great Rafael Nadal, as they announced the 22-time Grand Slam champion would be joining the club's board of directors
articles.body:
The club expressed its pride at the news the 22-time Grand Slam champion, and longtime Real Madrid fan, had taken the executive role on Wednesday.

Following the announcement, Nadal published a photo of himself as a child wearing a Real Madrid kit on his X account.

"I want to thank president Florentino Perez and the board who proposed me to be part of the board of directors at Real Madrid," Nadal wrote in the caption.

"I accepted this proposal with great excitement, a desire to learn and contribute everything I can."

It comes after Nadal, an honorary member of Real Madrid, took to social media earlier in 2026 to deny reports linking him to a possible candidacy for the club's presidency as "untrue".

Following Wednesday's announcement, Real Madrid paid homage to the 40-year-old, who retired from professional tennis in 2024, explaining Nadal's values aligned with the club's.

"Rafael Nadal, an honorary member of Real Madrid, is one of the greatest legends in the history of sport and one of the most admired and recognised Spanish athletes in the world," a club spokesperson said.

"For Real Madrid and for all Madrid fans, it is a great source of pride that a figure of his sporting and human stature, a benchmark of Spanish and world sport, will become part of our Board of Directors and contribute, from this position of responsibility, to the present and future of our club.

"Rafael Nadal has forged a legendary sporting career. But his figure represents much more than his successes: his talent, his constant drive to improve, his capacity for sacrifice, his competitiveness, his humility, his respect for rivals and team-mates, and his commitment to solidarity make him an example both on and off the court.

"All these values ​​are part of Real Madrid's identity, and Rafael Nadal has represented and defended them throughout his sporting life, becoming a role model for millions of people around the world."

articles.title: Mika Stojsavljevic: British teenager earns first WTA Tour win, beating Sofia Kenin in Hong Kong after only an hour's notice
articles.summary: Mika Stojsavljevic defeats 2020 Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin after being restored to tournament as a lucky loser; seventeen-year-old overcomes ranking gap of over 200 places; Stojsavljevic's fellow Brit Katie Boulter knocked out in second round, watch WTA Tour live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
The 17-year-old was given a spot as a lucky loser at the Hong Kong Open when Leylah Fernandez - runner-up to Emma Raudcanu at the 2021 US Open - withdrew.

Stojsavljevic, the world No 411, overcame a rankings gap of over 200 places as she beat Kenin 6-3 4-6 6-4 to set up a second-round meeting with Turkey's Zeynep Sönmez.

Stojsavljevic, who lost in the first round of qualifying in Hong Kong before her reprieve, said: "I only knew an hour before that I was going to be playing. I kind of just went out and swung. We didn't have much time to prepare.

"Obviously, I know she's a Grand Slam champion so it was never going to be an easy match but I believed in myself and it worked out."

Stojsavljevic lost her way from a set and 3-0 up against American Kenin but rebounded to win the deciding set in a match in which she struck six aces, six winners and converted six of 13 break points.

In 2024, the Londoner became the first Brit in 15 years to win the US Open girls' title, following Heather Watson's triumph back in 2009.

Stojsavljevic made her Billie Jean King Cup debut for Great Britain against Australia in Melbourne in April, defeating current world No 36 Talia Gibson in straight sets.

Elsewhere in Hong Kong on Wednesday, Stojsavljevic's compatriot Katie Boulter saw her season come to an end with a 7-5 6-4 defeat to American Claire Liu.

If Stojsavljevic is able to overcome Sönmez, she will play Liu in round three.

British No 1 Boulter had beaten Viktorija Golubic in straight sets in round one, despite an incident that "got under her skin".

articles.title: Dani Mérida se despide de París y de la temporada 2026
articles.standfirst: El madrileño cede ante Tommy Paul en el que era su último torneo del curso
articles.summary: El madrileño cede ante Tommy Paul en el que era su último torneo del curso
articles.body: Dani Mérida puede estar más que satisfecho con su 2026. El tenista de la capital ha cedido ante el estadounidense Tommy Paul por 6-1 y 6-1 en la segunda ronda del Masters 1000 de París, el que era la última cita de su calendario. Dani, que pasó con nota su debut en el TMS galo ante el argentino Sebastián Baez, hoy no ha podido con la maquinaria de Paul sobre pista cubierta. El americano necesitó 23 minutos para apuntarse la primera manga, en la que tan solo dejó escapar cuatro puntos. En el segundo set, una rotura en el juego inicial terminó de dibujar el camino en la pista 2 de la Défense Arena de París. Finalmente no jugará en Estocolmo la semana del 7 al 14 de este mes. Por lo tanto, el madrileño no volverá a competir hasta 2027. El español ha colmado una temporada llena de buenas noticias. Consiguió estrenar su palmarés alzándose con el ATP 250 de Umag; alcanzó la mejor posición de su carrera, subiendo hasta el escalón número 39 del ranking; y ya sabe lo que es jugar bajo los colores de su país en la Copa Davis, consiguiendo una victoria de mucho mérito ante el chileno Alejandro Tabilo en su propia tierra.

articles.title: Tennis great Rafael Nadal set to join Real Madrid board
articles.summary: The 22-time Grand Slam winner is to be ratified onto club’s board of directors.
articles.body:
Real Madrid are set to add a champion from another ⁠sporting arena to ⁠their boardroom as 22-time tennis Grand Slam winner Rafael Nadal’s appointment as a director is to be put to members for ⁠ratification, the club says.

The board agreed to submit the appointment to the General Assembly of ⁠Delegated Members. Nadal is already an honorary member of the club.

“It is a source of immense pride for Real Madrid and for all our supporters that a figure of his sporting and personal stature … is to join ‌our Board of Directors,” Real said in a statement on Wednesday.

The club highlighted Nadal’s sporting achievements, including 92 singles titles, two Olympic gold medals, five Davis Cup triumphs with Spain and the world number one ranking.

The club said his qualities beyond those honours – including humility, respect for opponents and commitment to charity – mirrored the club’s own.

“All ⁠these values form part of Real Madrid’s identity, and ⁠Rafael Nadal has embodied and championed them throughout his sporting career,” said the statement announcing his appointment at a board meeting on Tuesday.

“I would like to thank President Florentino Perez and the Board for ⁠inviting me to join the Board of Directors of Real Madrid,” he wrote on social media.

“I have ⁠accepted this invitation with great enthusiasm, keen to ⁠learn and to contribute as much as I can.”

Nadal, who retired from tennis in November 2024, has long been touted as a potential successor to Perez, ‌although he has played down the prospect.

Perez, 79, secured another four-year term in June after Real’s first contested presidential election in two decades.

More ‌than ‌a third of voting members backed challenger Enrique Riquelme, who opposed plans to bring outside investment into the member-owned club.

articles.title: Zverev cae en un debut trampa ante Musetti y se despide de París
articles.standfirst: El alemán, que dominaba el primer tie-break por 5-2, acaba cediendo en dos sets
articles.summary: El alemán, que dominaba el primer tie-break por 5-2, acaba cediendo en dos sets
articles.body: París ya no podrá disfrutar del campeón de 2024. Alexander Zverev, recién ascendido al número 1 del mundo, ha cedido en su debut en el Masters 1000 galo por 7-6 (5) y 6-2 ante el italiano Lorenzo Musetti. Hoy Sascha tenía enfrente un debut trampa ante el italiano, que está pasando por su mejor momento de la temporada con el título conseguido hace dos semanas en Lyon. Es el primero que levanta tras más de cuatro años de espera. En París ya acumula dos victorias de mérito. Ante el polaco Hubert Hurkacz y la reciente frente al campeón de dos grandes, Alexander Zverev. Es la segunda vez que el de Carrera se lleva un duelo ante un jugador que ocupa el primer puesto del ranking ATP. La primera fue ante Novak Djokovic en Montecarlo 2023. El alemán no estaba firmando un mal partido. No tenía el día con su servicio, pero salvaba las situaciones. Llegados al desempate inicial, Sascha comenzó mandando con mucha seguridad. Firmaba un 5-2 para posteriormente tener la opción de cerrarlo con dos servicios. Pero no fue así. Los fantasmas del pasado aparecieron, y un inspirado Musetti le dio la vuelta. Zverev no firmó ningún punto más en el tie-break. La segunda manga ya estaba decidida antes de empezar. El teutón salvó una bola de rotura en el juego inicial pero ya se le veía otra cara. Cabizbajo y sin intentar darle la vuelta, Musetti firmó el 'break' con 1-1 y eso le llevó hacia la tercera ronda del último TMS de la temporada. Sascha, por primera vez en dos años, ya que ganó en 2024 y fue semifinalista en 2025, disfrutará de más tiempo de descanso de cara a la Copa de Maestros de Turín (15 al 22). Una cita siempre marcada en rojo en el calendario del alemán. Ya ganó dos veces allí. En 2018 ante Djokovic y 2021 frente a Medvedev. Tras esto, le quedará la 'Final a 8' de la Copa Davis en Bolonia (24 al 29).

articles.title: La derrota de De Miñaur mantiene vivas las esperanzas de las ATP Finals para Jódar
articles.standfirst: El australiano cae ante Etcheverry y ya queda por debajo del madrileño en la 'race'
articles.summary: El australiano cae ante Etcheverry y ya queda por debajo del madrileño en la 'race'
articles.body: Ha saltado la sopresa en París. Tras el bombazo de la eliminación de Alexander Zverev, ha venido el de Alex de Miñaur. Pero este contiene buenas noticias para Rafa Jódar. El madrileño necesitaba sí o sí una derrota hoy de De Miñaur ante Tomas Etcheverry, y la ha conseguido. El argentino ha firmado la hazaña sobre la pista 2 de la Défense Arena de París por 7-6 (2) y 6-3 en favor de los intereses del recién ascendido al top10. Con el australiano fuera del camino, ya que tiene menos puntos que Jódar en la 'race' (3.234 acumula el español por los 3.170 de Alex), tan solo unas semifinales de Novak Djokovic y Taylor Fritz, y una final de Tommy Paul dejarían fuera a Rafa de las Nitto ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22). El serbio, que ocupa el decimoprimer puesto en la carrera a Turín con 2.940 puntos, está disputando su partido de segunda ronda ante el australiano Hijikata. Taylor Fritz, el primer americano en discordia con 2.900 puntos, jugará ante Molcan su segundo partido del torneo. En el caso de Tommy Paul, quien suma 2.825 puntos, ya está en la tercera ronda del TMS galo tras derrotar en 49 minutos a Dani Mérida.

articles.title: Zverev: "Siento que soy el único número uno en la historia del tenis que tiene que explicar por qué está bien que yo lo sea"
articles.standfirst: El alemán habla para los medios tras su derrota en París
articles.summary: El alemán habla para los medios tras su derrota en París
articles.body: Alexander Zverev ha querido dejar claro su enfado ante los medios tras ser eliminado en su debut frente a Musetti en el Masters 1000 de París. Y no ha sido principalmente por su derrota, donde asume que no ha tenido un buen desempeño: "Para resumirlo, él ha jugado realmente bien y yo he jugado bastante mal. No hay excusas", ha alegado el número 1 del mundo, que ha calificado el encuentro como "uno de mis peores partidos de los últimos meses". A la pregunta de si el alemán sintió presión por disputar su primer partido como número 1, fue cuando apareció el enfado de Sascha: "Conseguir el número uno del mundo es algo con lo que creo que sueña cualquier jugador, pero siento que soy el único número uno en la historia del tenis que tiene que explicar por qué está bien que yo sea número uno", afirmó Zverev. "Creo que merezco estar donde estoy, aunque hoy haya perdido", cerró el campeón de dos títulos de Grand Slam y actual número 1 del mundo. Parece que la perseverancia y el saber aprovechar tus oportunidades no se valora entre los aficionados.

articles.title: Medvedev cae a las primeras de cambio en el Masters 1000 de París
articles.standfirst: El ruso, que llegaba en un buen momento, no pudo con el peruano Ignacio Buse
articles.summary: El ruso, que llegaba en un buen momento, no pudo con el peruano Ignacio Buse
articles.body: El peruano Ignacio Buse consiguió la gesta de derrotar al ruso Daniil Medvedev en la segunda ronda del Masters 1000 de París, 6-4, 6-4, para clasificarse por primera vez en su carrera para los octavos de final de un torneo de esta categoría. El tenista de 22 años, actual número 33 del mundo, derrotó por vez primera a un tenista del top-10, un Medevedev, ganador de París en 2020 y actual número 5 del mundo, que llegaba en buena racha, con solo tres derrotas desde septiembre, periodo en el que se clasificó al menos para las semifinales de los cinco torneos que disputó y ganó los de Hangzhou y Almaty. El ruso es, además, el tenista que más partidos ha disputado sobre pista dura este curso, 41. No se amilanó el peruano, el primero en derrotar a un top-10 desde que en 2008 Luis Horna venciera al francés Richard Gasquet en Roma. Buse, el primer peruano que ganaba un partido en el Masters 1000 de parís, se medirá por un puesto en los cuartos de final contra el vencedor del duelo entre el ruso Karen Khachanov y el portugués Nuno Borges.

articles.title: Alexander Zverev 'annoyed' by reaction to him becoming world number one
articles.summary: After a defeat at the Paris Masters, Alexander Zverev complains that he is the only player who has had "to explain why it's OK" for him to be top of the rankings.
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev says he has been "annoyed" by the reaction to him becoming world number one.

The German, 29, claims he is the only tennis player who "has to explain why it's OK" for him to be top of the rankings.

Zverev lost to Italy's Lorenzo Musetti at the Paris Masters on Wednesday - his first match since becoming the ATP Tour's number one for the first time.

He has won his first two Grand Slams titles in 2026, but his success has come in a year in which Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner have struggled with injuries.

"I don't think anybody had to explain themselves as much as I had to do in the last couple of days, which for me, is annoying, to be honest," Zverev said.

Zverev has a 62-8 win-loss record against opponents ranked 11 and below in the world this year - but he has only won three of 12 matches against top-10 players.

Before this year's French Open, Sinner and Alcaraz had shared the past nine Grand Slam titles, with Sinner beating Zverev in last year's Australian Open final.

Zverev has lost in each of his 10 most recent meetings with Sinner, who has not played since Wimbledon after injuring his knee and has subsequently dropped to number two in the rankings.

He has also lost four of his past five matches against Alcaraz, who missed large parts of the season with a wrist injury.

"I was a bit annoyed, to be honest, because achieving the world number one status is something that every player dreams of," said Zverev, who won this year's French Open and US Open titles and lost to Sinner in the final of Wimbledon.

"But then I feel like I'm the only world number in tennis history that has to explain why it's OK for me to be world number one, which I find quite difficult, because I think I deserve to be where I am, even though I lost today."

Zverev did not specify which issues had been annoying him after going to the top of the rankings.

His ascent has led to previous accusations of physical abuse by two of his former partners being highlighted again.

Zverev has always firmly maintained his innocence and has insisted the allegations are baseless.

He was presented with the world number one trophy in Paris on Monday but, after receiving a bye through the first round, was beaten 7-6 (7-5) 6-2 by Musetti.

Looking at his performance on Wednesday, Zverev said: "To simplify it, he played really good and I played really bad.

"I think this was not a very good match from me, I think it might be one of the worst in the last couple of months."

articles.title: Djokovic dice adiós a París... y a las ATP Finals
articles.standfirst: El serbio cede ante Hijikata y le es imposible estar en Turín por cuarta vez en los últimos 20 años
articles.summary: El serbio cede ante Hijikata y le es imposible estar en Turín por cuarta vez en los últimos 20 años
articles.body: Novak Djokovic se une a la criba de favoritos en París. El campeón de 24 grandes se ha visto superado por el australiano Rinky Hijikata (83 del mundo) por 2-6, 6-3 y 6-3 para despedirse en la segunda ronda del Masters 1000 galo y poner fin a su misión de estar en las Nitto ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22). Por cuarta ocasión en las últimas 20 temporadas, 'Nole' no logra clasificarse para las ATP Finals. Ya ocurrió en 2017 por unas molestias en el hombro. En 2024 y 2025 fue baja por lesión. Un combativo Hijikata ha dado la sorpresa ante los 23.000 espectadores presentes en la pista central del último TMS de la temporada. Los mismos que no saben si volverán a ver al de Belgrado en la capital francesa. Novak abrió el partido con un gran primer set. La seguridad al servicio era notable desde las altas gradas de la Défense Arena de París, firmando un 79% de primeros dentro, y ganando el 84% de estos (16/19). Empezó con un 'break' a favor nada más salir de vestuarios, que acompañó de otro al séptimo juego del duelo para apuntarse la primera manga. Parecía todo decidido. Hijikata, a priori, no tiene las armas para combatirle de tú a tú al considerado mejor jugador de todos los tiempos. La historia fue diferente, ya que el australiano, a base de resistencia y de 20 golpes ganadores, rompió el saque de Djokovic para colocarse 5-3 y servicio. Lo cerró en blanco, y la suerte se decidiría en el tercer y definitivo set. Después de seis juegos sólidos, Hijikata dictó sentencia con un 'break' para firmar el 4-3 en el marcador. Fue el impulso que necesitaba para confirmar la sexta sorpresa del día. Tras las derrotas de Zverev, Medvedev, Tiafoe, De Miñaur y Tien, también caía el siete veces campeón del torneo, Novak Djokovic. Esta derrota pone fin a la temporada del serbio. La final en el Australian Open, las semifinales en Wimbledon y el título en Pekín, han sido sus mayores hitos. Acabará el año fuera del top10 por primera vez desde 2017. Esto aumenta las opciones del madrileño de estar en la cita de fin de año de Turín. Solo tendrá que esperar a que los americanos Taylor Fritz y Tommy Paul no alcancen las semifinales y la final, respectivamente.

articles.title: Alcaraz - Michelsen en directo | Última hora de Paris Masters 1000 en vivo hoy
articles.summary: ALCARAZ - MICHELSEN: 7-6(4), 6-3 Hasta aquí este directo, muchas gracias por seguir en MARCA el debut de Carlos Alcaraz en París. Antes de despedirnos
articles.body:
Última hora del Alcaraz - Michelsen en directo:

Carlos Alcaraz regresa a la competición tras su flamante victoria en el ATP 500 de Viena en una final en la que derrotó a Alex de Miñaur por 6-1 y 6-4. El murciano sumó el vigésimo octavo torneo de su palmarés como profesional y el cuarto del presente curso, a pesar de haberse perdido más de cuatro meses de competición por la lesión en la muñeca derecha.

La cita esta semana es en el Masters 1000 de París y el primer rival del español en la capital gala es el estadounidense Alex Michelsen . Alcaraz, número tres del ranking, se impuso a Michelsen en el único cara a cara entre ambos en la primera ronda del reciente Open 500 de Tokio . El americano, verdugo este ayer de Jiri Lehecka (6-7, 6-2 y 6-4) , es el 35 del ranking a sus 22 años.

Esta campaña, Michelsen alcanzó los cuartos de final del US Open , derrotado por su compatriota Frances Tiafoe. Por su parte, Carlos sigue afinando en pista dura bajo techo en busca de una puesta a punto que le haga llegar en las mejores condiciones a las dos citas más importantes de este mes, las ATP Finals y las finales de la Copa Davis.

A día de hoy Carlitos ya parece haber olvidado su lesión y está a pleno rendimiento, aunque explicó en la rueda de prensa de ayer en el multiusos de La Defense que tuvo dudas sobre si regresaría a su nivel: "Estuve mucho tiempo alejado de las pistas y tuve mucho tiempo para pensar y sentir. Hubo momentos en los que estaba seguro de que iba a volver a mi mejor nivel y otros en los que dudé de mí mismo , no voy a mentir, momentos en los que dudé de si podría volver a pegar la derecha a mi máximo nivel, al cien por cien, de si iba a estar físicamente a tope otra vez".

articles.title: ATP Paris Masters: Novak Djokovic eliminated from ATP Finals race as world No 1 Alexander Zverev also suffers shock exit
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic fails to qualify for season-ending ATP Finals after shock defeat in French capital, while world No 1 Alexander Zverev also exits Paris Masters but Carlos Alcaraz wins; You can watch the ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports this week
articles.body:
The 39-year-old, who also failed to make the 2017 edition due to a elbow injury, needed a run to the semi-finals to keep himself in with a chance of clinching a spot at the season-ending showpiece in Turin.

Djokovic, a seven-time champion in Paris, started well against 25-year-old Australian Rinky Hijikata, the world No 83, but faded badly in a 2-6 6-3 6-3 defeat.

With two places still available for the season-ending championship, Djokovic needed a run to the semi-finals in Paris to stay alive in his hopes, but his exit leaves the door open for the remaining contenders, including 12th-placed Taylor Fritz and 13th-placed Tommy Paul.

Hijikata told Sky Sports : "It took a lot. I was getting outplayed in the first set and had to hang tough.

"In the end I was glad I maintained my level and trusted myself in the big moments. I felt I had to take it to him and play aggressive."

Analyst Ryan Harrison, speaking to Sky Sports' Gigi Salmon, said: "Novak didn't really play poorly at all. This was Hijikata absolutely firing on all cylinders.

"After that opening set, Novak was controlling most the match, particularly behind his serve, but Rinky an unbelievable effort off the forehand side that was blistering. Just three forehand winners in the first set but he then poured them on for sets two and three."

Carlos Alcaraz started his title bid for a first trophy at the event with victory over Alex Michelsen 7-6 (7-4) 6-3.

The Spanish second seed will take on Matteo Berrettini next after the Italan defeated home hope and 2024 finalist Ugo Humbert 7-6 (7-3) 7-5.

'I deserve to be where I am' - Zverev suffers Musetti defeat

Alexander Zverev became the first male player in the history of tennis to lose in straight sets on his debut match as world No 1.

The 29-year-old German, who won the French and US Opens this year, was elevated to top spot in the ATP rankings for the first time on Monday.

However, he blew a 5-2 lead in a first-set tie-break on his way to a surprise 7-6 (7-5) 6-2 defeat by Italy's Lorenzo Musetti at the Paris Masters.

Speaking in his press conference, Zverev said: "To put it simply, he played really well and I played really badly. It was perhaps one of my worst matches in the last few months.

"I was a bit annoyed the last couple of days because achieving the world No 1 status is something that every player dreams of. But then I feel like I'm the only world No 1 in history who has to explain why it's normal for me to be No 1, which I find quite difficult because I deserve to be where I am, even though I lost today.

"I don't think anyone has had to explain themselves as much as I have in the last couple of days, which is annoying."

The 29-year-old, who climbed to No 1 on Monday, suffered a surprise defeat days after losing to Australia's ​Alex de Minaur in the Vienna Open ‌semi-finals.

Musetti, a former world No 5, seized the initiative by winning six of ​the final seven points of the opening-set tiebreak before taking command of the second set.

The 24-year-old Italian broke Zverev for a ​2-1 lead and struck again to move ⁠5-2 ahead on his way to ⁠victory.

"It's pretty shocking the level I was able to play in front of (Zverev), who was serving really well, especially in the first set," Musetti, 24, said in his on-court interview.

"It was really close. It could have gone both ways. The key was to stay there at 5-2. I played five great points in a row."

The win continued a ⁠resurgence for Musetti, who has been hampered by ​injuries throughout the 2026 season. His toughest ​setback came at the Australian Open, where he retired ​while leading 24-time Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic by two ⁠sets in their quarter-final clash.

In other second-round shocks, Frances Tiafoe wasted four match points in a 6-3 1-6 7-6 (11-9) loss to Frenchman Quentin Halys .

Tiafoe's defeat meant Arthur Fils qualified for the ATP Finals. He is the first Frenchman to reach the event since Gael Monfils in 2016.

Fourth-seeded Daniil Medvedev also went out after losing 6-4 6-4 to Ignacio Buse .

articles.title: Novak Djokovic: Serb's season over as defeat in Paris means he will miss ATP Finals
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic is out of the race to qualify for the ATP Finals in Turin after a second-round defeat by qualifier Rinky Hijikata at the Paris Masters.
articles.body:
Novak Djokovic is out of the race to qualify for the ATP Finals in Turin after a second-round defeat by qualifier Rinky Hijikata at the Paris Masters.

It means Djokovic, 39, has failed to qualify for the event for only the second time in the past 20 seasons when fit.

The Serb likely needed to reach the semi-finals in Paris to qualify, although the draw had appeared to open up for him after two of his rivals for a place fell earlier in the day.

Despite a good start, Djokovic was unable to repel Australian world number 83 Hijikata in a 2-6 6-3 6-3 defeat.

As Hijikata lifted his level at the end of the second set and throughout the decider, Djokovic, who appeared laboured and to be struggling physically, produced a series of errors, bringing an end to his season.

Djokovic said his plan for the next few weeks is "just rest".

"He was switched on, I wasn't serving as well and he was just playing out of his mind, honestly. He was not missing and keeping the ball low and just a terrific performance.

"He played really amazing tennis and it was my fault to let the control of the match go."

Zverev annoyed by reaction to becoming world number one

Death threats for Briton Burrage on WTA Tour return

Despite reaching the final of the Australian Open and the semi-finals of Wimbledon, Djokovic has not reached the quarter-final in any of this year's Masters 1000 events.

He won the last of his 24 Grand Slam titles at the US Open in 2023.

Qualifying for Turin would have given him a chance to win a record-extending eighth title at the season-ending championships.

Instead, only Americans Taylor Fritz and Tommy Paul remain in contention to take the final two places currently held by Frances Tiafoe and Rafael Jodar.

Djokovic had not failed to qualify when fit since 2017.

Tiafoe's chances were taken out of his hands earlier on Wednesday when he fell to a 6-3 1-6 7-6 (11-9) defeat by Frenchman Quentin Halys.

Australian Alex de Minaur then failed to take advantage as he lost 7-6 (7-2) 6-3 to Argentine Tomas Martin Etcheverry. A run in Paris could have secured De Minaur's qualification.

Elsewhere, world number one Alexander Zverev and fourth seed Daniil Medvedev, both of whom have already qualified for Turin, were also beaten.

Zverev said he was "annoyed" by the response to him becoming world number one after a straight-sets loss to Lorenzo Musetti, while Medvedev was beaten 6-4 6-4 by Peruvian world number 33 Ignacio Buse.

Fritz teetered on the brink of elimination but came through a decisive third-set tie-break to win 6-7 (6-8) 7-5 7-6 (7-5) against 78th-ranked Alex Molcan of Slovakia.

Earlier, Paul beat Spain's Daniel Merida 6-1 6-1, while Spain's Carlos Alcaraz - now the highest seed remaining - beat American Alex Michelsen 7-6 (7-4) 6-3.

After his triumph in Beijing, which ensured he would win at least one title for the 21st year in a row , Djokovic's season has rather fizzled out.

But playing four tournaments after the US Open, having previously admitted it is really only the Grand Slams which motivate him, suggests he is ready to tackle the 2027 season head-on.

Djokovic was a finalist at the Australian Open at the age of 38, but failed to reach the quarter-finals in eight of his eleven tournaments this year.

He reached the Wimbledon semi-finals, where he was outplayed by eventual champion Jannik Sinner, but fell in the third round of the French Open and the first round in New York.

That is a noticeable deterioration in his results - and it is only going to get harder, with his 40th birthday fast approaching in May.

articles.title: Jodie Burrage receives WTA support after social media abuse following Chennai Open defeat
articles.summary: Britain's Jodie Burrage is receiving support from WTA staff at an event in India after being sent death threats on social media.
articles.body:
Britain's Jodie Burrage has been receiving support from WTA staff at an event in India after being sent death threats on social media.

Burrage, 27, was bombarded with abusive online messages when she was beaten in her first WTA Tour singles main-draw match in 16 months on Tuesday.

On Wednesday, she won in the last 16 of the Chennai Open doubles alongside Robin Montgomery of the United States.

"Protecting players and the wider tennis family from online threats and abuse is a key priority for the WTA," the governing body told BBC Sport.

"We have WTA staff on the ground in Chennai offering Jodie support, along with our wider player welfare and Threat Matrix team."

Burrage shared a story on her Instagram account that showed the direct messages she had been sent following a 3-6 6-3 7-5 loss to India's Vaishnavi Adkar.

"Nice welcome back to tour. I remember why I left," Burrage wrote.

Burrage tagged the WTA into the post, asking when action will be taken to combat abuse. Other players, including Germany's Eva Lys, showed solidarity with the former world number 85.

Death threats for Briton Burrage on WTA Tour return

Is enough being done to protect players?

The WTA insists it is taking a "proactive approach" to protecting female players from abuse.

The Threat Matrix system, which uses artificial intelligence-led detection, can identify people behind the accounts that threaten players, enabling investigations to take place and potentially leading to legal action.

Female players were subjected to more than 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media last year, according to data from the service.

"Through Threat Matrix, a system we established in 2023, delivered by Signify Group alongside World Tennis, we identify, investigate and take action against those responsible," the WTA added.

"This includes reporting abusive content for removal, escalating serious cases to law enforcement and supporting action to prevent real-world harm.

"As much of the abuse players receive comes through direct messages, the WTA has offered Jodie additional support.

"These include a private channel to report abusive direct messages, and moderation that hides abusive comments on public channels before she sees them."

In 2024, a report from Signify found that angry gamblers were behind 48% of posts which were deemed to be abusive.

They were responsible for 42% of verified abuse in 2025 and 59% of cases of serious abuse.

The WTA is working with several gambling companies in a programme that flags abuse from gamblers in real time, allowing the operator to take direct action against those targeting athletes.

The company is then able to flag, restrict or suspend the account.

Mhairi Maclennan, chief executive of the Kyniska Advocacy, which supports female athletes, believes there is "still not enough being done" to protect athletes across the board.

"I'm afraid it is all too common for athletes who have public profiles to receive this type of abuse," she told BBC Radio 5 Live's Drive programme.

"Whether they have won or lost, a lot of the athletes we speak to report they have received abuse - whether death threats or rape threats - because of their public profile and because sports like tennis are tied to betting.

"Sports need a healthier relationship with betting agencies. Ultimately sports need money but we need to be looking at what betting is doing to individual athletes and looking after their welfare."

articles.title: Alcaraz derrota a Michelsen y esquiva la escabechina de favoritos en París
articles.standfirst: El español vence por 7-6(4) y 6-3 en un trabajado partido el mismo día que se despiden Zverev, Djokovic y Medvedev
articles.summary: El español vence por 7-6(4) y 6-3 en un trabajado partido el mismo día que se despiden Zverev, Djokovic y Medvedev
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha debutado en la segunda ronda del Masters 1000 de París con una trabajada victoria frente a Alex Michelsen por 7-6(4) y 6-3, en una hora y 41 minutos. El español ha salido airoso en un día extraño preñado de numerosas sorpresas, empezando por las derrotas de Zverev y Djokovic. Esta es la decimosexta victoria en otros tantos partidos contra tenistas más jóvenes que él en duelos de la ATP. Era la segunda vez que el murciano y el espigado estadounidense (1,93) se veían las caras en poco más de un mes, tras la sufrida victoria de Carlitos (7-6, 4-6, 6-1) en su estreno en el ATP 500 de Tokio, en un duelo con once roturas de servicio en el que Michelsen se mostró especialmente agresivo en su juego. Alcaraz tardó cinco juegos en tomarle el pulso al partido pero en cuanto destapó el tarro de las esencias logró una primera rotura de servicio con una dejada marca de la casa. El encuentro se ponía de cara, o eso parecía, porque el estadounidense lograba de inmediato un contrabreak aprovechando varios errores no forzados del tenista de El Palmar. Carlos volvió a la carga con cinco iguales pero falló un par de derechas aparentemente fáciles que le hubieran permitido disponer de unas valiosas pelotas de break. Así las cosas, la primera manga desembocaba en un tiebreak que debía marcar el devenir del duelo, sobre todo si el español lo ganaba. Una muerta súbita que empezó de la peor manera posible, con Michelsen adelantándose con un peligroso 1-4 al que el español respondía con rabia, dos certeros saques y dos derechas ganadoras que daban la vuelta al marcador (5-4). Un buen saque abierto que el americano devolvía a la red daba por finalizada una primera manga que se había alargado casi una hora. La segunda mantuvo la misma tónica, con una primera pelota de rotura en el séptimo juego que, afortunadamente, Michelsen no logró rentabilizar. Con todo, el partido estaba en el alero, porque Alcaraz alternaba sus habituales genialidades con errores no forzados. En el siguiente juego, un golpe de suerte del español -un punto regalado por la red- que descentró momentáneamente al estadounidense marcaría el destino del partido, aunque Alcaraz tuvo que meter un gran revés cruzado para apuntarse el 5-3. Carlos necesitó dos pelotas de partido para cerrar la contienda, tras fallar inicialmente una derecha sencilla. Un buen saque al cuerpo que Michelsen no pudo devolver acababa con las esperanzas del americano, que sigue sin ganar a un 'Top 5' en su carrera. El de París es uno de los tres Masters 1000 que aún no ha ganado Alcaraz -los otros son Canadá y Shanghái-. De hecho, el español no tenía un registro positivo hasta hoy, pues con su triunfo suma seis victorias y cinco derrotas en sus seis participaciones, con los cuartos de 2022 como tope. El rival mañana (19.00) en octavos del español será Matteo Berrettini, que venció por 7-6(3), 7-5 al francés Ugo Humbert. Será el quinto duelo entre Carlos y el italiano, con un balance de 3-1 para el murciano.

articles.title: Alcaraz: "Lo de Nadal directivo del Madrid me parece una locura, me alegra por él"
articles.standfirst: El tenista murciano, que habló tras su victorioso debut en París, es un reconocido aficionado del club blanco
articles.summary: El tenista murciano, que habló tras su victorioso debut en París, es un reconocido aficionado del club blanco
articles.body: Ttras su victorioso debut en el Masters 1000 de París frente a Alex Michelsen, Carlos Alcaraz consideró "una locura" la noticia de que Rafa Nadal entrará en la directiva del Real Madrid y aseguró que tendrá una ocasión de verle cuando vaya al Santiago Bernabéu. "Me parece una, es una locura, la verdad. Cuando lo he visto me he alegrado, me alegra muchísimo por él. Es alguien que tiene el fútbol como manera de vida, es un gran apasionado del fútbol, un gran apasionado del Real Madrid", aseguró en París, poco después de clasificarse para octavos de final del Masters 1000 de la capital francesa. "Yo creo que el hecho de que Florentino (Pérez) haya contado con él para que esté en la directiva es bueno, es algo increíble, le deseo todo lo mejor a Rafa, que es lo que se merece y espero poder verlo cuando vaya a ver al Real Madrid", afirmó el murciano, también aficionado del club blanco.

articles.summary: El murciano domina los cara a cara contra el italiano pero no se cruzan desde 2023
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz vuelve este jueves a la pista en el Masters 1000 de París con el objetivo de seguir avanzando en uno de los torneos más importantes del tramo final de la temporada. El murciano se mide al italiano Matteo Berrettini en un duelo de octavos de final que promete intensidad y espectáculo sobre la pista rápida de La Défense Arena. El número uno español afronta una nueva prueba de nivel después de superar con éxito su estreno en la capital francesa, donde derrotó a Alex Michelsen por 7-6(4), 6-3. Enfrente tendrá a un rival de sobra conocido por el murciano y que atraviesa un buen momento de forma. El italiano lleva un acumulado este año de 22-18 y no se ha anotado ningún título. En Roland Garros alcanzó los cuartos de final y se trata de su mejor actuación de la temporada. En los cara a cara se impone por 3-1 el murciano (número 3 del ranking) al italiano (número 43). Su último enfrentamiento se produjo en Wimbledon 2023; en pista dura bajo techo se vieron en una ocasión, en Viena en 2022 y ganó el jugador nacido en Roma hace 30 años. El encuentro entre Carlos Alcaraz y Matteo Berrettini, correspondiente a los octavos de final del Masters 1000 de París, está previsto para este jueves 5 de noviembre en el primer turno dentro de la sesión nocturna del torneo, es decir, a las 19.00 horas. El partido de la segunda ronda del Masters 1000 de París entre Carlos Alcaraz y Matteo Berretini se podrá seguir a través de Movistar +. articles.title: Beach Tennis transforma momentos de lazer em experiências esportivas e integração | G1
articles.standfirst: Com estrutura dedicada à modalidade e a realização do tradicional Jurema Open, Jurema Águas Quentes reúne esporte, diversão e bem-estar em meio à natureza.
articles.summary: Com estrutura dedicada à modalidade e a realização do tradicional Jurema Open, Jurema Águas Quentes reúne esporte, diversão e bem-estar em meio à natureza.
articles.body:
Mais do que uma atividade física, o beach tennis é uma oportunidade de unir movimento, diversão e convivência. Cada vez mais popular no Brasil, a modalidade conquistou espaço entre pessoas de diferentes idades e perfis, tornando-se também uma excelente opção para quem deseja aproveitar as férias de maneira ativa. Em Jurema Águas Quentes , o esporte faz parte de uma proposta de lazer que combina experiências, qualidade de vida e contato com a natureza.

Praticado em quadras de areia, com raquetes específicas e uma bola semelhante à de tênis, o beach tennis mistura elementos do tênis tradicional, do badminton e do vôlei de praia. A dinâmica descontraída, aliada à possibilidade de jogar em duplas, faz da modalidade uma atividade que estimula o condicionamento físico, a coordenação motora e a interação social.

Em Jurema Águas Quentes, os apaixonados pelo esporte encontram uma estrutura preparada para a prática. São 13 quadras de beach tennis distribuídas entre os dois resorts do complexo: dez no Jardins de Jurema Convention & Termas Resort e três no Lagos de Jurema Termas Resort . A infraestrutura permite que hóspedes aproveitem a modalidade durante a estadia, seja para manter a rotina de atividades físicas, aprender a jogar ou simplesmente compartilhar momentos descontraídos com amigos e familiares.

Jurema Open: esporte que aproxima pessoas

O incentivo ao beach tennis também ganha destaque com a realização do Jurema Open , campeonato que já se consolidou como um dos eventos esportivos importantes do calendário regional. Ao longo das edições, a competição cresceu em participação e visibilidade, passando de 80 jogadores na primeira edição para uma expectativa de aproximadamente 300 atletas na sétima edição.

O campeonato reúne competidores de diferentes localidades, incluindo participantes do Paraná, Santa Catarina e Mato Grosso do Sul, em disputas que valorizam tanto o desempenho esportivo quanto o espírito de integração.

Além das partidas, o Jurema Open proporciona uma programação que amplia a experiência dos participantes. Lounge, bares, espaços de recuperação e massagens, música, piscinas, shows e jantares temáticos ajudam a transformar o campeonato em um encontro que vai além das quadras.

As categorias contemplam diferentes públicos, incluindo disputas masculinas, femininas e infantis, incentivando a participação de atletas com diferentes experiências no esporte.

Uma experiência que vai além das quadras

A proposta de Jurema Águas Quentes é proporcionar experiências diversificadas em um mesmo destino. Por isso, a prática esportiva encontra espaço ao lado de outras atividades de lazer, das piscinas de águas termais às experiências de relaxamento e entretenimento disponíveis no complexo.

Para quem gosta de manter o corpo em movimento mesmo durante as férias, o beach tennis representa uma alternativa dinâmica e divertida. Já para os iniciantes, é uma oportunidade de conhecer uma modalidade acessível e descobrir uma nova paixão.

Com infraestrutura esportiva, eventos que estimulam a prática da modalidade e uma programação diversificada, Jurema Águas Quentes reforça que descansar também pode significar experimentar coisas novas, movimentar o corpo e criar boas histórias.

Seja em uma partida descontraída durante a hospedagem ou na emoção das disputas do Jurema Open , o beach tennis é mais uma maneira de aproveitar tudo o que o complexo oferece.

articles.title: Rafa Jódar saca la calculadora para estar en las ATP Finals de Turín
articles.standfirst: El madrileño necesita que Fritz no esté en semifinales de París y Paul no se meta en la final
articles.summary: El madrileño necesita que Fritz no esté en semifinales de París y Paul no se meta en la final
articles.body: Lo que se veía de color negro el pasado martes, cuando Rafa Jódar cedió en la segunda ronda del Masters 1000 de París con Casper Ruud, ahora ya no lo es tanto. Jódar, que dependía de cuatro jugadores para estar por primera vez en su carrera en unas ATP Finals, ahora lo hace de dos, con las derrotas de Alex de Miñaur y Novak Djokovic. Taylor Fritz y Tommy Paul tienen la llave para que el joven de Leganés acompañe a Carlos Alcaraz del 15 al 22 en la cita de maestros de Turín. Para que eso pase se tiene que dar una doble carambola: que Fritz no esté en las semifinales del TMS de París y que Paul no se mete en la final. El primero disputa este jueves los octavos ante el local Arthur Fils, ya clasificaco entre los ocho mejores del curso. Y tendría unos hipotéticos cuartos con Alcaraz, segunda cabeza de serie del cuadro. El murciano tendría que ganar antes a Matteo Berrettini. Paul se las verá en la cuarta ronda con otro local Quentin Halys. En cuartos tendría al ganador del duelo entre Ben Shelton y Arthur Rinderknech. Y en semifinales podría topar con Lorenzo Musetti, verdugo de Alexander Zverev, número uno mundial. A sus 20 años, Jódar aspira a convertirse en el primer jugador de la historia que se clasifica para las ATP Finals en su primera temporada como profesional. Un nuevo récord que está a punto de caer de su lado. Con la clasificación estos días en París de Flavio Cobolli y Fils tan sólo quedan dos plazas para el 'round robin' de los maestros de la campaña 2026. Rafa es ahora mismo noveno de la Race 2026, con 3.234 puntos, por detrás de Frances Tiafoe, que cuenta con 3.390. Fritz es undécimo, con 2.950 y Paul, decimotercero, con 2.825.

articles.title: Las WTA Finals más picantes: "Perdí el respeto por ella, es una buena chica pero necesita madurar"
articles.standfirst: La estadounidense Pegula raja de la rusa Andreeva en pleno entrenamiento
articles.summary: La estadounidense Pegula raja de la rusa Andreeva en pleno entrenamiento
articles.body: Las WTA Finals de Indian Wells llegan con un extra de picante después de que Jessica Pegula, la número cinco del ranking, fuera captada el miércoles por las cámaras y los micrófonos de ambiente rajando sin piedad de la rusa Mirra Andreeva, la tercera raqueta en féminas y flamante campeona de Roland Garros. "Perdí el respeto por ella. Es una buena chica, pero necesita madurar. No sé si es porque no sabe cómo manejarlo", le dice Pegula a su entrenador en mitad de una práctica en el Tennis Garden de Indian Wells. La millonaria Pegula, hija de Terry Pegula, propietario y presidente de los Buffalo Bills (NFL) y Buffalo Sabres (NHL) y propietario de Rochester Americans (AHL), Buffalo Bandits (NLL) y Rochester Knighthawks (NLL), también se refiere al trato que Andreeva le dispensa a la española Conchita Martínez, su preparadora: "Si yo fuera su entrenadora y mi jugadora acaba de jugar cuatro grandes juegos, va ganando 4-0, se enoja conmigo y me persigue... Yo le diría que no me hable así. Es una diva y hay que bajarle los humos". Jessica, de 32 años, y Andreeva, de 19, se encuentran en el desierto californiano para disputar la cita de maestras de la WTA. Ambas han caído en grupos distintos y sólo podrían cruzarse a partir de las semifinales.

articles.title: El estado de forma de Berrettini refleja el malestar en el equipo italiano de la Copa Davis
articles.standfirst: El romano se ha quedado fuera de la convocatoria para las finales de Bolonia en beneficio de Darderi
articles.summary: El romano se ha quedado fuera de la convocatoria para las finales de Bolonia en beneficio de Darderi
articles.body: Fue dar la convocatoria de Italia para la fase final de la Copa Davis y sacar la mejor versión de Matteo Berrettini. El romano, ausencia sensible entre los cinco convocados por su conocido distanciamiento con Lorenzo Musetti (los dos residen en Montecarlo y comparten agente), se coló la semana pasada en los cuartos de Viena y este jueves disputa los octavos del Masters 1000 de París contra Carlos Alcaraz. En ese intervalo de tiempo, Luciano Darderi, el tenista natural de Villa Gesell (Argentina), que completa la convocatoria de la escuadra transalpina, ha ganado un partido, a su compatriota Matteo Arnaldi, en Viena. El buen momento de Berrettini, que puede jugar indistintamente los individuales y el dobles en la Copa Davis, señala aún más la crisis interna en el seno de los campeones del mundo. Matteo, a sus 30 años y en el puesto 43, presenta unos números en la máxima competición por países de 12 partidos individuales ganados por dos perdidos. Tiene dos victorias y otras tantas derrotas en dobles. Aunque lo más significativo son sus nueve triunfos seguidos, coincidiendo con dos de las tres Ensaladeras de Italia. A eso se añade que Simone Bolelli y Andrea Vavassori, el mítico dúo transalpino, han anunciado su separación como pareja a partir de 2027. Antes de la serie con Corea del Sur, del miércoles 25 de noviembre, todas las miradas apuntan al capitán Filippo Volandri.

articles.title: Alcaraz se mete en cuartos sin jugar tras la retirada de Berrettini
articles.standfirst: El italiano, que era su rival en octavos del Masters 1000 de París, anuncia que no jugará por el dolor que le acompaña desde hace varios días en el brazo
articles.summary: El italiano, que era su rival en octavos, anuncia que no jugará por el dolor que le acompaña desde hace varios días en el brazo
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz salta directamente a los cuartos de final del Masters 1000 de París tras el anuncio de Matteo Berrettini de que no jugará los octavos por una lesión. El italiano lo explicó en sus redes sociales: "El dolor en el brazo que llevo conmigo desde hace algunos días no me deja jugar esta noche. En los próximos días realizaré todas las pruebas necesarias para comprender mejor lo que está sucediendo". Tras vencer en primera ronda Brandon Nakashima por 6-4, 3-6 y 7-6 (8) en un apretado partido, luego se impuso a Hugo Umbert por 7-6 (3) y 7-5 para citarse este jueves con Alcaraz. El choque, que ya no se jugará por su retirada, estaba previsto para abrir la jornada de tarde en París. Berrettini estaba en un buen momento tras haberse metido en los cuartos de Viena y pisar los octavos en París, pero se había quedado fuera del equipo italiano para la Final a 8 de la Copa Davis en Bolonia. Alcaraz se medirá en cuartos al ganador del partido entre Arthur Fils y Taylor Fritz, previsto para cerrar este jueves la sesión de noche, pero que ha sido adelantado a las 19.00 horas. La baja de Berrettini dará al murciano un día de descanso extra con respecto a su próximo rival. Una victoria permitiría a Carlitos superar su mejor resultado en el Masters 1000 de París ya que su tope son los cuartos alcanzados en 2022 cuando se retiró por lesión en el 'tie break' del segundo set ante Holger Rune. Alcaraz, además, puede convertirse en el mejor aliado de Rafa Jódar. El madrileño entraría en las ATP Finals si Tommy Paul no llega a la final en París y si Fritz no pisa las seminales. Si este último saca adelante su encuentro de octavos ante Fils, sería entonces Alcaraz el que le podría apartar de la carrera hacia Turín en beneficio de Jódar.

articles.title: Mika Stojsavljevic: British teenager beaten in Hong Kong a day after first WTA Tour win of her career
articles.summary: Mika Stojsavljevic, 17, had shocked former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin on Wednesday after being restored to tournament as lucky loser; Brit now inside the world's top 400; Hong Kong Open runs until Sunday, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Stojsavljevic, 17, shocked former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin on Wednesday after being restored to the tournament as a lucky loser with only an hour's notice.

The Londoner was beaten 7-6 (7-5) 6-4 by Turkish world No 67 Zeynep Sonmez on Thursday in a little over two hours.

Stojsavljevic entered the Hong Kong Open ranked 411th in the world but is now just outside the top 350 in the live rankings following her victory over Kenin.

In 2024, she became the first Brit in 15 years to win the US Open girls' title, following Heather Watson's triumph back in 2009.

Stojsavljevic made her Billie Jean King Cup debut for Great Britain against Australia in Melbourne in April, defeating current world No 36 Talia Gibson in straight sets.

Sonmez's reward for defeating Stojsavljevic is a quarter-final against Katie Boulter's conqueror Claire Liu.

Three-time Grand Slam quarter-finalist, Sorana Cîrstea, is the top seed in Hong Kong, with Alexandra Eala the second seed.

Jódar es uno de los cuatro jugadores aspirantes a una de las dos plazas restantes para las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22). Ahora mismo estaría dentro del 'round robin' como noveno de la Race 2026, por detrás de Frances Tiafoe, también eliminado en el TMS galo. Pero siguen avanzando Tommy Paul y Taylor Fritz. El primero, de hecho, se ha clasificado este jueves para la antepenúltima ronda. Paul ha acabado con la resistencia del galo Quentin Halys, por 7-6(3) y 6-4, en 1 hora y 35 minutos. Espera ahora a su compatriota Ben Shelton (3), verdugo de Arthur Rinderknech, por 3-6, 6-4 y 7-6(5). Tommy, por la parte alta del cuadro, tendría unas hipotéticas semifinales con Lorenzo Musetti, verdugo de Alexander Zverev. Paul, 309 puntos por detrás de Jódar, necesita alcanzar la final para adelantar al joven de Leganés. Por su parte, a Fritz le valdrían las semifinales. Pero hoy se mide a la primera raqueta de Francia, Arthur Fils, clasificado para Turín, y le esperaría Carlos Alcaraz en los cuartos.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz through to Rolex Paris Masters quarter-finals after Matteo Berrettini withdraws injured
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz has been handed a free passage through to the quarter-finals of the Paris Masters following the withdrawal of Matteo Berrettini; watch the ATP Paris Masters live on Sky Sports this week, with the WTA Finals in Indian Wells starting on Sunday
articles.body:
The pair had been due to play on Thursday evening in the French capital but Berrettini has suffered another injury setback, pulling out due to pain in his arm.

Alcaraz, who is chasing his fifth tour-level trophy of the season in the French capital, will face home favourite Arthur Fils or Taylor Fritz in the last eight at the ATP Masters 1000 event.

The Spaniard will be bidding to reach the semi-finals on the indoor hard courts of Paris for the first time in six appearances.

An official social media announcement from the tournament read: "Matteo Berrettini has to withdraw from the Rolex Paris Masters. Wishing you a speedy recovery Matteo. Carlos Alcaraz is qualified for the quarter-finals."

Berrettini posted his statement of his own in Italian on Instagram stories, which translated as: "Hi all, unfortunately the pain in my arm that I've had for a few days won't allow me to take the court tonight.

"In the next few days I will have all the necessary tests to better understand what this is. Thank you all for the support and affection you show me every day on and off the court. Mat."

Fils, who will take on Fritz in the night session, became the first French player to qualify for the ATP Finals since Gael Monfils in 2016 earlier this week.

Fritz is currently 11th in the Race To Turin and still has a chance to qualify, although the American knows he must defeat both Fils and Alcaraz to reach the semi-finals to keep his hopes alive.

Alcaraz holds a 39-5 record for the season so far and has already qualified for the ATP Finals in Turin later this month having won four titles this year - Australian Open, Qatar Open, Japan Open and last week's Vienna Open.

articles.title: Jessica Pegula calls Mirra Andreeva 'diva' after Indian Wells practice session
articles.summary: The WTA says it takes "full responsibility" after private comments Jessica Pegula made to her coach about Mirra Andreeva were live-streamed by a courtside microphone.
articles.body:
The Women's Tennis Association says it takes "full responsibility" for not telling players there were microphones on practice courts after private comments Jessica Pegula made to her coach about fellow player Mirra Andreeva were live-streamed.

The session at Indian Wells, California, was streamed by the WTA before its Tour Finals start on Sunday.

In a private conversation with her coach Mark Knowles, world number five Pegula described Andreeva as "a diva".

The American could also be heard saying the French Open champion "needs to be humbled" and her coach Conchita Martinez encourages her behaviour.

Pegula's agent, Chris McCormack, said she had been "completely unaware" the conversation could be heard by courtside microphones, "let alone live-streamed to the public".

"Naturally it's been an unfortunate situation for everyone involved," McCormack told BBC Sport.

"Jess has since been in direct contact with those involved, which she felt was important to do personally rather than through the media."

YouTube streams of Wednesday's practice sessions at Indian Wells have since been removed by the WTA, but the footage had already been shared on social media.

It is understood the microphones were only intended to capture the sounds of rallies and not any conversations on court, and there will be no audio on future videos.

"The WTA takes full responsibility for failing to inform our players and their teams that microphones, in place to give fans a livestream of the players' practice, were active on the courts at the WTA Finals," a statement read.

"We sincerely apologise for failing to meet our responsibility to ensure players and coaches were properly informed."

Pegula, who is a member of the WTA players' council, also praised Andreeva, saying the world number three is "wonderful" and "smart".

The season-ending WTA Finals, being held at Indian Wells for the first time, run until 15 November.

Pegula's representative and the WTA have been approached for comment.

In a separate incident, world number one Elena Rybakina appeared to have an angry exchange with her coach before a practice session with Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova.

Some of the audio is unclear, but Pegula can be heard describing how Andreeva and Martinez complained throughout the session, even though Andreeva won every game.

Pegula: "Conchita's always been very nice to me, but I've lost a little respect for her because I'm like, this girl - I think she's a nice girl - she's just a diva. She needs to be humbled. She needs to be [inaudible] putting her in her place; [inaudible] stand up to her."

Spaniard Martinez - the 1994 Wimbledon champion - began working with Andreeva in April 2024. Andreeva reached the Wimbledon quarter-finals last year and claimed her first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros in June.

Pegula: "Conchita pokes her and eggs on her behaviour."

Knowles: "She needs somebody to put her in her place. Once she gets that, I think she'll be really good. I mean, she's already really good. Look how she moves."

Pegula: "She moves like a cat. She's wonderful. She's got the perfect serve. She's smart. She anticipates well."

Pegula, who has not won a Grand Slam, then compared Andreeva to world number four Coco Gauff. The American was also 19 when she won her first Grand Slam. Now 22, she has won two majors.

Pegula: "It's so funny how you see her and then you see Coco's mentality. If she had Coco's mentality, she'd be better than her."

Pegula: "The serve, everything, all-around, and she moves just as good. But like mentally, she's..."

Pegula and Andreeva are in different groups at the WTA Finals but could meet in the semi-finals or final.

Pegula's group opponents are Gauff, Rybakina and Noskova, and the latter pair's practice session at Indian Wells was also live-streamed.

Australian and US Open champion Rybakina appears to remonstrate with coach Stefano Vukov as they walk to the net, saying: "Stay here. I'm talking to you. Can you stand here?"

They shared a few more words, which are inaudible, before going to the other side of the court together to greet Noskova and her team.

Vukov was suspended by the WTA in February 2025 following an independent investigation into his behaviour towards Kazakhstan's Rybakina. He returned to her team that August.

Pegula was among the players to complain about additional behind-the-scenes cameras at the Australian Open in January.

The semi-finalist described the filming as an "invasion of privacy" that needs to be "cut back".

"You just feel like you're under a microscope constantly," she said.

articles.title: Jodie Burrage: British tennis player calls on social media platforms to hold people accountable for sending abusive messages
articles.summary: Jodie Burrage opens up to Sky Sports about the online abuse and death threats she received after her defeat at the Chennai Open; Burrage says most abuse comes from tennis gamblers who have lost money; Warning: This article contains details some readers may find distressing
articles.body:
Burrage, who was playing her first WTA Tour match since Wimbledon last summer, received death threats and online abuse following a first-round defeat at a tournament in India on Tuesday .

The 27-year-old shared a raft of abusive messages sent to her Instagram account after a gruelling 3-6 6-3 7-5 defeat by India's Vaishnavi Adkar. Alongside the video, Burrage wrote: "Nice welcome back to the tour. I remember why I left."

It has been three years since the WTA - in partnership with Wimbledon, World Tennis and the United States Tennis Association - launched the AI-led Threat Matrix service, which aims to identify and tackle online abuse against players and officials.

Burrage was visibly shaking and had her blood pressure and oxygen levels checked as well as ice rubbed on her arms and legs during the match in sweltering conditions. She was able to resume the contest but lost the final game to love.

"I received quite a few messages on social media," Burrage told Sky Sports . "Abusive messages and things that you shouldn't be getting after (a match) or that anyone should ever have to deal with in that matter anyway.

"I got them after the match and it didn't make it easier, that's for sure.

"With what happened in the match as well, me not feeling my best, my blood pressure actually tanked at the end of that third set.

"So obviously people were concerned back home. I was on my phone in the physio room with the doctors and replying to people, telling them I was OK, and then I was seeing these messages come up on my phone.

"It's probably not the best thing to be on your phone, but in that circumstance, I kind of had to be.

"I didn't actually look at most of the messages. I screenshot some to send to someone to show them and then decided to post them [in a video] for awareness of what it's like after a tough loss."

Burrage: 'It's a lot bigger than just me'

Data from Threat Matrix showed female tennis players faced more than 12,000 abusive posts and messages on social media in 2025, with angry gamblers responsible for 42 per cent of verified abuse and 59 per cent of serious abuse.

"It's not just after losses. If I win a match, I normally get some sort of abuse as well, with the way that tennis works. You can bet on a lot of things," explained Burrage.

"I think that's where the anger comes from; it's probably losing money. And the messages say it as well. They want their money back or shouldn't have bet, or I lost the money.

"I've spoken to so many people, especially in the last few days. It's not easy after a tough loss like that to receive those kind of messages. I normally deal with it pretty well.

"At the end of the day, we're pretty used to receiving it. So you get used to batting it away and not thinking twice about it. But I shouldn't have to - that's the point!

"It's amazing that a lot of people got in touch and were so up in arms, saying, 'I can't believe you receive this'.

"I'm kind of glad it got the awareness. I guess I've got people talking because I do believe something needs to happen. Trying to change it is the most important thing.

"It's all sports, sports people and whoever's on social media as well. Beyond tennis and sports people, it's social media in general, I think. So it's a lot bigger than me, than other people, than tennis."

Burrage is one of a number of players to have previously spoken out about the level of abuse received and a failure of the governing bodies and social media companies to tackle it effectively.

A report released in July said 66 per cent of serious abusive posts and comments identified by the programme were removed, while 35 accounts linked to 12 individuals were escalated to law enforcement, but Burrage, who had a career-high WTA singles ranking of No 85 in 2023, feels more can be done.

"What hasn't been done is having an ID connected to your social media account. I feel like that's an easy fix. I could be being naive with that. But then it makes people accountable, and it makes people accountable for what they post and what they say.

"If actions want to be taken, then they can, especially with threats. When someone's safety is being compromised."

The WTA has offered additional support to Burrage, although the Brit fears the governing body for women's tennis can only do so much, with the greater emphasis on social media platforms to make more of an effort in combating death threats and abuse.

She said: "I think the WTA doing everything they can. I'm currently speaking to a few people I've been told to get in touch with about all things. So I'll wait to see if that helps.

"For me, it's more the platforms themselves. I think more could be done to try and limit it and to try and change it and make people accountable for what they say to other people online."

Having made her first singles appearance on the tour in Chennai since a first-round defeat at Wimbledon in 2025, Burrage is also focusing on a solid pre-season block of training before returning to action in the new year.

"Everything I'm doing now is to build up for my 2027," she said.

"I really feel I need to build my body back up. I got sick over grass [court season] this year, which I'm still feeling the effects of.

"So I'm wanting to put a really good block in, which I'm kind of starting now, to be honest with the stuff off the court. Everything is for a good start in 2027, where I'll go to Australia.

"I always love it there. To start in a place that I've played well in and where I'm hopefully in a good spot. It's exciting and I'm excited to get back out there."

In response to Burrage highlighting the abuse she received earlier this week, a WTA spokesperson told Sky Sports News : "Protecting players and the wider tennis family from online threats and abuse is a key priority for the WTA.

"We have WTA staff on the ground in Chennai offering Jodie support, along with our wider player welfare and Threat Matrix team.

"Through Threat Matrix, a system we established in 2023, delivered by Signify Group alongside World Tennis, we identify, investigate and take action against those responsible.

"This includes reporting abusive content for removal, escalating serious cases to law enforcement and supporting action to prevent real-world harm.

"As much of the abuse players receive comes through direct messages, the WTA has offered Jodie additional support, including a private channel to report abusive direct messages, and moderation that hides abusive comments on public channels before she sees them.

"Threat Matrix is also reporting the abuse Jodie received to the platforms, and investigations are underway to identify those responsible.

"Where the abuse is linked to betting, they will be added to the Bad Actor programme so betting operators can act against their accounts."
